places.name: Big Spring State Park
places.coord_point: TPWD-printed park GPS point (entrance or HQ not labelled on the page)
nearby: Big Spring (the park's own city, per Wikipedia lead)
places.blurb: Day-use park on arid plains. Civilian Conservation Corps crews reworked about 300 acres in 1934-35. Has a group pavilion.
places.status_note: TPWD page says 'This park has active alerts' and links an alert page; alert text not retrieved. TPWD lists it as a day-use park, open 8 a.m. to sunset.
places.notes: Name candidates (ten): Alidade (chosen), Hesper, Kestrel, Pleiad, Plumbline, Almagest, Dipper, Meridian, Tellurian, Vesta. Coordinates: TPWD page prints Latitude 32.232288 and Longitude -101.490728 (confirmed in the raw HTML). Wikipedia (Big Spring State Park (Texas) infobox) gives 32.23222, -101.49056, about 20 m away; TPWD used. Acres: TPWD prints 382 acres (used); Wikipedia 381.99. Camping: TPWD calls it a day-use park with a group pavilion; no campsite pages exist and the raw HTML has only the site-wide Camping and Lodging menu, so camping is false. The brief's /stay path returns 404 for every TPWD park; TPWD camping details live under /fees-facilities/ subpages. Nearby: only the city is named in the sources read; a second sourced nearby item was not found. County Howard from Wikipedia (TPWD does not print a county).

places.name: Copper Breaks State Park
places.coord_point: TPWD-printed park GPS point (entrance or HQ not labelled on the page)
nearby: Quanah (about 21 km north of the park, per DarkSky place page)
Medicine Mound (named as a nearby town on the TPWD page)
places.blurb: Canyon breaks and two small lakes 21 km south of Quanah. A DarkSky Park since 2014, with star walks dating to 1996.
places.status_note: TPWD page says 'This park has active alerts'; alert text not retrieved. Reservations recommended for camping and day use, not stated as required. Page says the park often reaches capacity.
places.notes: Coordinates: TPWD prints Latitude 34.112176 and Longitude -99.743296 (confirmed in the raw HTML). Wikipedia infobox gives 34.11139, -99.75250, about 0.9 km away, under the 2 km threshold; TPWD used. Acres: TPWD prints none; Wikipedia gives 1,898.8 (used). DarkSky place page lists land area 7.82 km2 (about 1,932 acres), a different measure; not used. DarkSky designation confirmed on darksky.org's own page (fetched with a browser user agent after WebFetch returned 403): 'Designated 2014 Category Dark Sky Park'. TPWD dark-skies page also lists it as an International Dark Sky Park (no year). Camping, from TPWD /fees-facilities/campsites and horse-sites pages: Comanche area, 24 sites with 30/50 amp and water hookups, $20 nightly (counted as rv_hookups; the page does not use the word RV); Kiowa area, 11 water sites marked 'Tent only (no RVs)'; Big Pond Equestrian area, 14 sites marked 'Tent only' with horses; 6 primitive hike-in sites with no water; group camps at Big Pond (5 sites) and Cottonwood (4 sites); 2 overflow sites. Cabins, screened shelters, backcountry and dispersed are not mentioned.

places.name: Fort Parker State Park
places.coord_point: TPWD-printed park GPS point (entrance or HQ not labelled on the page)
nearby: Mexia (city near the park, per Wikipedia)
Groesbeck (town named in Wikipedia history; no distance given)
places.blurb: Navasota River park with a 750-acre lake near Mexia. Electric and tent campsites, cabins, screened shelters and a scout group camp.
places.status_note: TPWD page says 'This park has active alerts'; alert text not retrieved. Reservations recommended, not stated as required.
places.notes: Coordinates: TPWD prints Latitude 31.592347 and Longitude -96.526655 (confirmed in the raw HTML). Wikipedia infobox gives 31.60361, -96.55083, about 2.6 km away, past the 2 km threshold; the official TPWD point is used, and the disagreement is flagged here. Acres: TPWD prints only the lake (750 acres); Wikipedia gives 1,458.8 (used). County and nearest town from Wikipedia. Camping, from TPWD /fees-facilities/campsites: 24 'Campsites with Electricity' (water and 30 amp, up to 8 people, $20 nightly, counted as rv_hookups since the page does not use the word RV); 1 tent-only electric site; 10 tent-only water sites; a Scout group camp for up to 50 (sponsored youth group, primitive toilet). Cabins from the lodging page: 2 cabin sites, 8 per site, no beds or bathrooms. Screened shelters from the shelters page: 8 shelters, 12 by 18 feet, no beds, with outlet, light and picnic table.

places.name: Huntsville State Park
places.coord_point: TPWD-printed park GPS point (entrance or HQ not labelled on the page)
nearby: Huntsville (the park is six miles southwest of the city, per Wikipedia)
Sam Houston National Forest (named in Wikipedia lead; no distance given)
places.blurb: Pine-shaded park six miles southwest of Huntsville, with a 210-acre lake, 160 campsites, cabins and screened shelters.
places.status_note: TPWD page says 'This park has active alerts'; alert text not retrieved. Reservations recommended for camping and day use, not stated as required.
places.notes: Coordinates: TPWD prints Latitude 30.628404 and Longitude -95.525921 (confirmed in the raw HTML). Wikipedia infobox gives 30.61944, -95.53056, about 1.1 km away; TPWD used. Acres: TPWD prints only the 210-acre Lake Raven; Wikipedia gives 2,083 (used). County Walker and nearest town from Wikipedia. Camping, from TPWD /fees-facilities/campsites: 23 Full Hookup (RV) sites at $25; 77 Campsites with Electricity 'for tents and/or RVs'; 54 Campsites with Water, no electric. The site classes add to 154, while the main page says 'choose from 160 campsites'; both figures are kept as written. Cabins page: 2 cabin sites, 8 per site, no bathrooms (restrooms with showers nearby). Screened shelters page: 28 shelters, 12 by 18 feet, 8 per site; minimum two-night stay on Friday and Saturday nights. Group: group pavilion or hall per the main page.

places.name: Lake Tawakoni State Park
places.coord_point: TPWD-printed park GPS point (entrance or HQ not labelled on the page)
nearby: Wills Point (11.2 miles south of the park, per Wikipedia)
Dallas (about 50 miles west, per TPWD page)
places.blurb: 376 acres of oak forest beside a 37,879-acre lake near Wills Point, with full-hookup, electric, tent and primitive group sites.
places.status_note: TPWD page says 'This park has active alerts'; alert text not retrieved. Reservations recommended, not stated as required.
places.notes: Coordinates: TPWD prints Latitude 32.841871 and Longitude -95.993667 (confirmed in the raw HTML). Wikipedia infobox gives 32.84861, -96.00000, about 0.95 km away; TPWD used. Acres: TPWD says 376 acres of oak forest (used); Wikipedia 376.3. The 37,879-acre figure is the lake, not the park. County Hunt is from Wikipedia (infobox and lead); TPWD does not print a county and I did not check the county boundary against the point, so verify this county before it is published. Camping, from TPWD /fees-facilities/campsites: Spring Point Full Hookup, 16 sites at $24, 'RV & tent allowed'; Spring Point electric, 16 sites at $22, 'RV & tent allowed'; White Deer Reach electric (30 amp), 44 sites at $20; 2 accessible electric sites; one group camp for up to 48 people, no vehicles, about a 100-yard hike, no water, $42. The main page's 'primitive group campsite (for up to 48 people)' is the basis for primitive. Cabins and screened shelters are not mentioned.

places.name: Mother Neff State Park
places.coord_point: TPWD-printed park GPS point (entrance or HQ not labelled on the page)
places.blurb: Leon River park near Moody. Isabella Neff donated its first six acres in 1921. Full-hookup RV sites and a historic CCC lodge.
places.status_note: Gate at the south end closed indefinitely. The 15 tent sites are 'currently closed due to flood damage'. The Breezeway pavilion is closed for flood damage. Swimming and fishing not allowed because of river conditions. Active-alerts text not retrieved.
places.notes: Coordinates: TPWD prints Latitude 31.334236 and Longitude -97.467917 (confirmed in the raw HTML). Wikipedia infobox gives 31.32167, -97.46917, about 1.4 km away; TPWD used. Acres: TPWD prints only the six acres donated in 1921; Wikipedia gives 259 (used). County Coryell from Wikipedia (infobox and lead). Camping, from TPWD /fees-facilities/campsites and lodging: 20 Full Hookup sites with water, sewer and 30/50 amp electric, $25 nightly; 15 tent sites currently closed; the 'Lodge (CCC Cabin)' has 4 bedrooms and 2 bathrooms, sleeps up to 16 including 8 sleeping outside in tents, $200 Friday to Sunday and $160 Monday to Thursday. The group page lists no overnight group campsites: Rock Tabernacle pavilion (capacity 250) and Breezeway pavilion (capacity 50, closed for flood damage). TPWD distances: Gatesville 23 miles, Temple 25 miles, Waco 32 miles.

places.name: Resaca de la Palma State Park
places.coord_point: TPWD-printed park GPS point (entrance or HQ not labelled on the page)
nearby: Brownsville (the park is in the city, per Wikipedia)
South Padre Island (about a 40-minute drive, per TPWD page)
places.blurb: Former Rio Grande channel in Brownsville where private vehicles are barred. Visitors ride a tram or walk or bike in from the visitor center.
places.status_note: TPWD page says 'This park has active alerts' twice, with a screwworm alert link and a park alert link; alert text not retrieved. 'We do not allow private vehicles in the park.' Park says it often reaches capacity. Day-use reservations recommended.
places.notes: Coordinates: TPWD prints Latitude 25.996275 and Longitude -97.5712694 (confirmed in the raw HTML); the Wikipedia infobox matches exactly. Acres: TPWD prints none; Wikipedia gives 1,200 (used). County Cameron from Wikipedia. Camping: the TPWD page names only group sites (group-facilities page linked, not fetched, so overnight use of groups is unconfirmed); the raw HTML has only the site-wide Camping and Lodging menu. Camping is therefore set to false. Visitor center hours 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; park open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. (TPWD). Adult day-use fee $4 daily (TPWD). A second Wikipedia header coordinate (25.9867, -97.5649) does not match the infobox and was not used.

places.name: Big Thicket National Preserve
places.coord_point: NPS-printed visitor center coordinates (Big Thicket National Preserve Visitor Center, 6102 FM 420, Kountze)
nearby: Kountze (visitor center town, per NPS address)
Village Creek State Park (named in an NPS search summary; the NPS page itself was not fetched, so second-hand)
places.blurb: Forested preserve of scattered units in Southeast Texas. No developed campgrounds: backcountry camping only, with a free permit.
places.status_note: Fall and winter camping (October 1 to February 28) is limited to areas that do not allow hunting. The NPS page lists only the Turkey Creek Unit and Neches River Corridor for that period. Some areas are closed, including land within 1,000 feet of the Pitcher Plant Trail. Limits: 14 consecutive nights, 28 nights per year, groups of 8.
places.notes: Coordinates: the NPS directions page prints 'Visitor Center Lat./Long. Coordinates: 30.458251, -94.387285' (confirmed by fetch). The Wikipedia infobox point 30.54750, -94.34000 is the whole-preserve centroid, about 10 km away, and was not used. Visitor center street address 6102 FM 420, Kountze; the NPS footer gives a different mailing address (6044 FM 420, Kountze, TX 77625), unexplained on the page. Acres: Wikipedia infobox 113,122 (NPS page not checked for acres). County Hardin is from the Wikipedia body text ('all of Hardin County', with parts of Polk and Tyler). Camping: NPS camping page URL returned 404; the backcountry page was used instead. Permits are free, issued at the visitor center, with advance permits up to 14 days ahead. The NPS search summary said a newer page lists more fall-winter camping areas (Woodlands Trail area, Canyonlands, Loblolly); that conflicts with the fetched page and was not used. The unit named on the directions page is the Lance Rosier Unit.

places.name: Angelina National Forest
places.coord_point: Boykin Springs Recreation Area (Forest Service-printed campground point; the Zavalla ranger district office has no printed coordinates)
nearby: Zavalla (ranger district office, 111 Walnut Ridge Road, per Forest Service page)
Sam Rayburn Reservoir (named as a geographic feature on the Forest Service page)
Lufkin (forest supervisor's office, 2221 N. Raguet Street, per Forest Service page)
places.blurb: East Texas national forest across parts of four counties. Boykin Springs campground has RV-length sites and a CCC picnic shelter.
places.status_note: Forest Service page lists Harvey Creek Boat Ramp as 'Closed due to damage' and the SFA Experimental Forest toilet as closed (trail open). Boykin Springs status not stated on the page.
places.notes: Office: Angelina National Forest Ranger District, 111 Walnut Ridge Road, Zavalla, TX 75980, phone (936) 897-1068, Forest Service page (no printed coordinates). The point used is the printed Boykin Springs coordinate (31.0591, -94.2775) from the campground page. The Wikipedia infobox point 31.26861, -94.41194 is a forest-level point about 23 km away and was not used. Acres: Wikipedia 153,180 (the Forest Service page does not print acres). County 'Jasper' is NOT printed on the Forest Service page: it comes from a search summary of that page and needs verification against a county boundary before publication, because the point sits near the Angelina and Jasper line. The Wikipedia lead says the forest lies in parts of San Augustine, Angelina, Jasper and Nacogdoches counties. Boykin Springs facilities from the campground page: camping trailer sites ('9 sites can accommodate RVs up to 24 feet long') without hookups ('no sites with water hookups'); single sites at $10; group sites at $25 per day; bathhouse with flush toilets and hot showers; picnic shelter for up to 74 with reservations required; horses and pack animals not allowed. Reservations by phone 877-444-6777 or the recreation.gov link. Other forest recreation areas and dispersed camping are per a second-hand MVUM summary, not verified, and are not reflected in the point's camping kinds.
